docs.title: HelixRF USB Display HUD
docs.text:
The HelixRF USB Display HUD is a large touch display for your radio. It reads the radio over USB and shows the frequency, mode, meters and the spectrum scope with waterfall on a 10.1-inch screen. You can change band, mode and filter from the screen, decode FT8, FT4, CW and RTTY, and follow the radio from a web browser on your home network.

This manual covers all firmware versions unless a section says otherwise.

Main screen: meters, frequency, radio functions and the spectrum scope with waterfall.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A compatible display, bought separately. HelixRF sells the app only. The screenshots in this manual are from the Guition JC8012P4A1C, a 10.1-inch, 1280 × 800 touch display. The list of compatible displays and radios is in the product description and grows over time.
  • A PC with Chrome or Edge and a USB cable, to install the app the first time
  • A supported radio connected by USB (see Setup)
  • A 2.4 GHz WiFi network for the web interface, firmware updates and the network radio server
  • Your activation code, emailed within 72 hours of payment

docs.title: What is included
docs.text:
Feature Without a licence With a licence or the trial Frequency, mode, meters, spectrum scope and waterfall Yes Yes Band, mode, filter and function control from the screen Yes Yes Settings, on the screen and in the web interface Yes Yes FT8 / FT4 / CW / RTTY decoding 2-minute preview after each power-on Yes Web live display 2-minute preview after each power-on Yes Network radio server (for wfview and similar software) No Yes

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Five steps take you from a new display to a working HUD: download the app, install it on the display, connect to WiFi, activate your licence and connect your radio.

docs.title: 1. Download
docs.text:
Download the firmware from the link in the product description, or from My account → Downloads on helixrf.com.

The app is a binary firmware file (.bin) that you install on the display.

File Use it for helixrf_hud_full.bin First install over USB, at address 0x0. It holds the boot loader, the partition table and the app. helixrf_hud.bin Updates over WiFi from the web interface. App only.

Use the right file

Never write helixrf_hud.bin at address 0x0. It is the app only, and the display will not start. Use helixrf_hud_full.bin for the first install.

docs.title: 2. Install
docs.text:
The display must have an ESP32-P4 chip of silicon revision 3 (v3.1 or later). Check your display's documentation if you are not sure.

Use the flashing tools at helixrf.com, or any flashing tool from Espressif that supports ESP32-P4 silicon revision 3.

  1. Connect the display to your PC with a USB cable. Any USB port on the display works for this first install.
  2. Open the flashing tool in Chrome or Edge. Other browsers cannot reach a serial port.
  3. Click Connect. When the browser asks, pick the display's serial port and allow access.
  4. If the tool asks for the chip, select ESP32-P4.
  5. Set the flash address to 0x0 and choose helixrf_hud_full.bin.
  6. Click Program and wait until the tool reports it is done.
  7. Unplug the USB cable and power the display again. The HelixRF logo appears, then the main screen.
Command-line install with esptool

With Espressif's esptool:

esptool.py --chip esp32p4 write_flash 0x0 helixrf_hud_full.bin

Add -p COMx (Windows) or -p /dev/ttyUSBx (Linux) if more than one serial port is connected.

Display does not connect?

Put the display in download mode as its manual describes (on most ESP32 boards: hold BOOT, press and release RESET, then release BOOT), and click Connect again.

Once the HUD is running and on your WiFi, later versions are installed from the web interface. See Update the firmware.

docs.title: 3. Connect to WiFi
docs.text:
The web interface, firmware updates and the network radio server need WiFi. The display and radio control work without it.

Settings → WiFi. The QR code opens the web interface on your phone.
  1. On the main screen, tap SETTINGS (bottom right).
  2. Open the WiFi tab.
  3. Tap Scan, then pick your network from the list. Or type the name in Network (SSID).
  4. Type the Password.
  5. Tap Save & Connect.

When the HUD is connected, the tab shows Connected to your network and the signal strength in dBm. The WiFi icon at the top of the main screen turns green.

To open the web interface, scan the QR code with your phone, or type http://helixrf-hud.local/ in a browser on the same network. If that name does not work on your computer, use the IP address shown under the QR code.

docs.title: 4. Activate your licence
docs.text:
The HUD has a Device ID, made from the hardware. Your licence key is an activation code (108 characters) made for that Device ID, so it works on that display only.

Your unique licence key is emailed within 72 hours of successful payment. Payment and invoicing are handled by our Merchant of Record, Paddle.com Market Ltd. Nothing is shipped.

Settings → Licence. The Device ID is blurred in this picture.
  1. Tap SETTINGS, then the Licence tab.
  2. Note the Device ID (for example K7Q2-M9XD) and send it to HelixRF: type it in the Device ID field at checkout when you order, or email it with your order number to s21rc@helixrf.com.
  3. When the activation code arrives, type it in the activation code field. Dashes, spaces and upper or lower case do not matter.
  4. Tap Activate. The status changes to show the licence is active.

You can also activate in the web interface: open the Licence page, paste the code in Activation code and click Activate. Pasting is easier than typing 108 characters on the screen.

Licence page in the web interface.

If the code is not accepted, the HUD shows one of these messages:

Message What to do Enter the activation code first. The field is empty. Type or paste the code. That is not an activation code. It should be 108 letters and digits. Part of the code is missing or extra characters were added. Copy it again from the email. The code contains a typing error. Please check it character by character. One character is wrong. Compare the code with the email. This code does not match this device's ID. The code was made for another Device ID. Check the Device ID you sent. The code is valid but could not be saved. Please try again. Tap Activate again. If it keeps failing, contact support.

No key after 72 hours?

Check your spam folder first, then contact us with your order number.

docs.title: 14-day trial
docs.text:
You can try all features for 14 days before you buy, with no registration. On the Licence tab (on the screen or in the web interface), tap Start 14-day trial. The status then shows the days left.

The trial can be started once. Without a licence or a running trial, decoding and the web live display each run for 2 minutes after every power-on; the network radio server is off.

docs.title: 5. Update the firmware
docs.text:
Firmware page in the web interface.
  1. Download the new helixrf_hud.bin (see Download).
  2. Open the web interface and click Firmware. Running shows the version now installed.
  3. Click Choose File and pick helixrf_hud.bin.
  4. Click Upload & install. The bar shows the progress, and the HUD restarts when the upload is done.

The new firmware must run for 90 seconds without problems before the HUD keeps it. If it fails, the HUD goes back to the previous version by itself.

Warning

Keep the HUD powered during the upload.

docs.title: 6. Connect your radio
docs.text: Continue with Setup.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text: The latest firmware is always available from My account → Downloads on helixrf.com. Install it from the web interface as described in Update the firmware.

docs.title: Latest
docs.text:
First release.

  • Main screen with frequency, mode, filter, split and tuner status, S / Po, SWR, ALC, Vd and Id meters, and the radio's spectrum scope with waterfall.
  • Three meter faces: Bars, Analog and Vintage.
  • Touch control: band, mode, filter and frequency panels, tap-to-tune on the scope, preamp, attenuator, AGC, noise blanker and noise reduction.
  • FT8, FT4, CW and RTTY decoding from the radio's USB audio, with DXCC country names for FT8 and FT4. CW has two decoders: NEURAL and CLASSIC.
  • Web interface: live mirror of the main screen with tap-to-tune, settings, licence and firmware update over WiFi.
  • Network radio server for wfview and similar LAN-radio software, with remote transmit off by default.
  • Licence activation by Device ID, and a 14-day trial.

docs.title: Supported radios
docs.text:
The HUD talks to Icom radios over CI-V on the radio's USB port. The list of compatible displays and radios is in the product description; radios are added gradually.

Choose the brand and model in Settings → Radio; the HUD then fills in the default CI-V address and baud rate for that model. The model list in the app:

Radio Connection Default CI-V address Icom IC-7300 USB (CI-V + audio) 94h Icom IC-7300MK2 USB (CI-V + audio) B6h Icom IC-705 USB (CI-V + audio) A4h Icom IC-7610 USB (CI-V + audio) 98h Icom IC-9700 USB (CI-V + audio) A2h Icom IC-905 USB (CI-V + audio) ACh Icom IC-7851 USB (CI-V + audio) 8Eh Icom IC-R8600 USB (CI-V + audio) 96h Yaesu FT-710 USB (CAT) — Kenwood TS-890S USB (CAT) —

Note

A model in this list is not necessarily confirmed compatible; check the product description. Yaesu and Kenwood radios are in the list for a later update that adds their CAT control.

Decoding uses the radio's USB audio (receive audio), so it needs a radio with a built-in USB sound card, such as the IC-7300.

docs.title: Connect the radio
docs.text:
1. Connect the radio's USB port to the display's high-speed USB port with a USB cable. Check your display's manual to find which port that is. (Any port works for installing the app; only the high-speed port works for the radio.)
  2. Switch the radio on. No driver is needed; the HUD finds the radio by itself.
  3. On the HUD, tap SETTINGS and open the Radio tab.
  4. Choose the Brand and Radio model.
  5. Check the CI-V address and USB baud. They must match the radio's menu (see below).
  6. Tap Apply.

The USB icon at the top of the main screen turns green when the radio answers.

Settings → Radio. The bottom of the tab repeats the radio menu settings. Setting What it does Brand Icom, Yaesu or Kenwood. Filters the model list. Radio model Sets the default CI-V address and baud rate for that model. CI-V address The radio's CI-V address. Use the model's default unless you changed it in the radio. USB baud Serial speed: 4800 to 115200. Must match the radio's CI-V USB baud rate. Serial format (web only) 8N1 or 8N2, for Yaesu and Kenwood radios.

docs.title: Radio menu settings
docs.text:
On the IC-7300, open MENU → SET → Connectors and set:

Radio menu item Setting Why CI-V → CI-V USB Baud Rate The same as USB baud on the HUD, or Auto 115200 is needed for the spectrum scope. CI-V → CI-V Transceive ON The radio reports changes made on its front panel. USB SEND / USB Keying OFF Transmit from the network goes over CI-V. MOD Input → DATA MOD USB Transmit audio from the network in the -D modes. Only needed for the network radio server.

docs.title: Network radio server (wfview)
docs.text:
The HUD can act as a network radio, so you can run wfview or similar LAN-radio software on a PC without a cable to the radio. It passes the radio's control, spectrum scope and audio (48 kHz) over your network. Needs a licence or the trial.

  1. In Settings → Radio, under Network radio server, type a Username and Password.
  2. Switch Server on.
  3. Tap Save. The line below shows Waiting for a client at the HUD's address, port 50001.
  4. In wfview, set Radio Connection to Network, Hostname to helixrf-hud.local (or the HUD's IP address), Control Port to 50001, the same username and password, and the codec to LPCM or uLaw.

The HUD uses UDP ports 50001 to 50003.

docs.title: Remote transmit
docs.text:
Allow remote transmit is off by default. While it is off, transmit (PTT) requests from the network are refused, so the PC can only listen.

When you switch it on:

  • Each transmission is limited to 3 minutes.
  • The radio is unkeyed if the network link drops.
  • The network icon on the main screen turns red while the network keys the radio.

Warning

Only allow remote transmit when you, or another licensed operator, can watch the station. You are responsible for every transmission.

For FT8 with WSJT-X on the PC, use wfview's virtual serial port or rigctld for CAT and PTT.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Open Settings → Status to see what the HUD sees: WiFi, the USB devices found, the CI-V link and the firmware.

Settings → Status with a working IC-7300: two USB devices (CI-V bridge and USB audio) and "radio OK". Symptom Fix USB icon red, USB host shows no devices Check the cable and that the radio is on. Use the display's high-speed USB port. Try another USB cable. USB devices listed, but no radio (CI-V shows no reply) Check USB baud and CI-V address match the radio's menu. Set CI-V Transceive to ON. Frequency shows but no spectrum scope Set CI-V USB Baud Rate to 115200 (or Auto) on the radio and USB baud to 115200 on the HUD. Decode page shows no audio The radio's USB audio codec must be listed under USB host in Settings → Status. FT8 / FT4 decodes nothing The clock must be right: FT8 needs UTC within about a second. The HUD sets its clock from the internet, so it needs WiFi. Display flickers or the radio's USB drops while a PC is also plugged into the HUD This is a ground loop between the PC and the radio. Unplug the PC, or use a USB isolator. The HUD reconnects to the radio by itself and counts the drops as USB resets on the Status tab. helixrf-hud.local does not open Use the IP address from Settings → WiFi instead. Some computers and phones do not support .local names. Touch is offset Run Calibrate touch in Settings → Display. See Using the app. wfview cannot log in Check the username and password in Settings → Radio, that Server on is set, and that the HUD has a licence or a running trial.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: Still stuck? Every HelixRF product includes free remote support. You can also use the contact page or email s21rc@helixrf.com. Tell us your Device ID, the firmware version (Settings → Status) and your radio model.

docs.title: Main screen
docs.text:
The main screen shows the radio at a glance. Most items are also buttons: tap them to change the radio.

Main screen with the Bars meter face.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text: Item Shows Tap to TX Red while the radio transmits. — Mode (for example USB-D) The radio's mode. -D means data mode is on. Open the mode panel. FIL1 / FIL2 / FIL3 The selected filter. Open the mode panel. SPLIT Amber while split is on. Switch split on or off. TUNE Green while the antenna tuner is on; TUNING while it tunes. Tap: tuner on or off. Touch and hold: start a tune (the radio transmits a carrier). USB icon Green: the radio is answering. Red: no radio or no CI-V reply. — WiFi icon Signal strength of the WiFi link. — Network icon Only shown when the network radio server is on. Grey: waiting. Blue: a client is connected. Red: the network is keying the radio. — Clock UTC, set from the internet. Shows --:-- until the clock is known. —

docs.title: Meters and frequency
docs.text: Item Shows Tap to S Signal strength, S1 to S9+60. Becomes Po (output power) while transmitting. — SWR, ALC Transmit meters. — Vd, Id The radio's supply voltage and drain current. — Frequency The main VFO frequency in MHz. Open the band panel. A/B The other VFO's frequency. Swap VFO A and B.

docs.title: Function chips
docs.text:
Chip Tap to P.AMP1 / P.AMP2 Step the preamp: off → P.AMP1 → P.AMP2 → off. (IC-9700 and IC-905: one preamp.) ATT Attenuator on or off (20 dB; 10 dB on the IC-9700 and IC-905). AGC-F / AGC-M / AGC-S Step the AGC: fast → mid → slow. NB Noise blanker on or off. NR Noise reduction on or off. PWR Shows the RF power setting. Display only. SPAN Shows the scope span. Display only. REF Shows the scope reference level. Display only.

A blue chip is on; a grey chip is off.

docs.title: Spectrum scope and waterfall
docs.text:
The scope shows the radio's own spectrum data. CENTER or FIX at the top left is the radio's scope mode. The white line marks the operating frequency.

Tap the spectrum or the waterfall to tune there (in 100 Hz steps).

The DECODE button opens the decode screen and SETTINGS opens Settings.

docs.title: Meter faces
docs.text:
There are three meter faces. Swipe left or right over the meter area (between the two orange lines) to switch. Choose the face shown at start-up in Settings → Display → Main screen face at start-up.

Face Look Bars Bar meters for S, SWR, ALC, Vd and Id (picture above). Analog A dark dial with one needle: S on receive, Po on transmit. Vintage The same dial with a warm, back-lit look.

Analog face.

Vintage face.

docs.title: Band, mode and frequency panels
docs.text: A panel opens over the meters. Tap anywhere else to close it; it also closes after 10 seconds without a touch.

docs.title: Band
docs.text:
Tap the frequency to open the band panel.

Band panel. The current band is orange.

Each button shows the band, the frequency and the mode you will go to. The HUD remembers the last frequency and mode you used on each band. For bands you have not used since power-on, it reads the radio's band stacking register. Only the bands your radio model has are shown.

Tap F-INP to type a frequency.

docs.title: Frequency keypad (F-INP)
docs.text:
Frequency keypad.
  1. Type the frequency. With a decimal point it is in MHz (14.074); without one it is in kHz (14074).
  2. Tap ENT to tune. ⌫ deletes one digit; CE clears the entry.

The now line shows the current frequency. Frequencies outside 30 kHz to 11 GHz show out of range.

docs.title: Mode and filter
docs.text:
Tap the mode or filter badge to open the mode panel.

Mode panel. Button Does LSB, USB, CW, CW-R, RTTY, RTTY-R, AM, FM Set the mode. DATA Data mode on or off (for example USB → USB-D). FIL1, FIL2, FIL3 Select the filter.

docs.title: Decode screen
docs.text:
Tap DECODE on the main screen. The decoder uses the radio's USB receive audio. Tap HUD to go back and Clear to empty the list.

Choose the mode with the buttons along the top: FT8, FT4, RTTY and CW. Greyed-out modes (JT65, JT9, WSPR, Q65, FST4, MSK144) are not available yet. The HUD remembers the last mode.

Decoding needs a licence or the trial. Without one, it runs for 2 minutes after each power-on, then shows Preview ended.

docs.title: FT8 and FT4
docs.text:
FT8 decoding.

The waterfall shows the audio passband (0 to about 3000 Hz). Each decode cycle adds lines to the list:

Column Shows UTC Start time of the cycle. dB Signal-to-noise ratio. DT Time offset in seconds. Freq Audio frequency in Hz. Message The decoded message. Entity The DXCC country of the sending station.

Messages are coloured: green for CQ calls, yellow for signal reports, orange for 73 and RR73. Messages with your own call sign (set in Settings → Station) are highlighted.

FT8 and FT4 need the correct time. The HUD sets its clock from the internet over WiFi.

docs.title: CW
docs.text:
CW decoding (top of the screen).

The status line shows the tone frequency, the speed in WPM, the signal-to-noise ratio and the audio level. The decoder follows the strongest signal near the radio's CW pitch.

  • Tap the waterfall on a signal to lock the decoder to that tone.
  • Tap AUTO to unlock it again.
  • NEURAL / CLASSIC switches between the two CW decoders. NEURAL gives far less junk text from noise; CLASSIC is the traditional decoder. Both do well on clean signals.

docs.title: RTTY
docs.text:
RTTY decoding (top of the screen).

The status line shows the speed (45.45 Bd), the mark and space tones, the signal-to-noise ratio, REVERSE when the radio is in RTTY-R, and the audio level. Tune the signal onto the mark and space tones shown.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Tap SETTINGS on the main screen. The tabs are on the left. Info opens the Info screen and HUD goes back to the main screen. Settings are saved in the HUD and kept after power-off.

Tab Use it to WiFi Connect to your WiFi. See Getting started. Station Set your own call sign. Radio Choose the radio and set up the network radio server. See Setup. Display Backlight, scope colours, meter face, touch calibration. Licence Activate a licence or start the trial. See Getting started. Status Check WiFi, USB, CI-V and firmware. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Station
docs.text:
Settings → Station.

Type your call sign in Own callsign and tap Save. Allowed characters are A–Z, 0–9 and /. FT8 and FT4 messages with your call sign are highlighted.

docs.title: Display
docs.text: Settings → Display. Setting What it does Backlight Screen brightness. Calibrate touch Starts the touch calibration (see below). Spectrum fill colour Colour under the spectrum trace: Blue, Cyan, Green, Amber, Orange, Red, Purple or Grey. Spectrum outline colour Colour of the trace line: Grey, Light, White, Cyan, Green, Yellow, Orange, or Off. Waterfall intensity Higher makes weak signals brighter in the waterfall. 50 % is neutral. Spectrum zoom ×1.0 to ×4.0. A taller trace makes small signals stand out. Main screen face at start-up Bars, Analog or Vintage meter. Spectrum peak hold Off, Short (1 s) or Long (3 s). Reset to default Puts the scope settings back to the factory values.

docs.title: Touch calibration
docs.text:
Touch works out of the box. If touches land in the wrong place, calibrate:

  1. Tap Settings → Display → Calibrate touch, or open http://helixrf-hud.local/calibrate in a browser.
  2. A cross appears in each corner in turn. Tap and hold the centre of the cross briefly, four times.

If nothing is touched for 45 seconds, the calibration is cancelled and the old settings stay.

Touch calibration, first of four points.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Settings → Status. Section Shows WiFi Connection, IP address, gateway, signal (RSSI), channel, MAC address, and whether the clock is synchronised (NTP synced). USB host The USB devices found. An IC-7300 shows two: the CP2102 USB-to-UART bridge (CI-V) and the USB Audio CODEC. CI-V Link state, radio address, baud rate, frequency, mode and meter values, frame counters and USB resets (automatic reconnects). Firmware Version, uptime, reason for the last restart, and free memory.

docs.title: Info screen
docs.text:
Tap Info in Settings.

Info screen. The Device ID is blurred in this picture.

It shows the firmware version, the Device ID and licence state, the web interface addresses, and the third-party software notices. Tap Settings to go back.

docs.title: Web interface
docs.text: Open http://helixrf-hud.local/ (or the HUD's IP address) in a browser on the same network. The menu at the top has Live, Home, Settings, Licence, Info and Firmware.

docs.title: Live
docs.text:
Live page in a desktop browser.

The Live page mirrors the main screen in your browser, and you can work it the same way:

  • Tap or click the spectrum or waterfall to tune.
  • Click the frequency for the band panel, and the mode for the mode panel.
  • Click P.AMP, ATT, AGC, NB or NR to switch them.
  • Bars, Analog and Vintage choose the meter face in the browser.
  • Setup opens the other web pages.

The status text next to Setup shows radio connected, or HUD offline - reconnecting... when the link drops. Up to two browsers can show the Live page at the same time. Needs a licence or the trial; without one it runs for 2 minutes after each power-on.

Live page with the Bars face.

Band panel in the browser.

The page also works on a phone or tablet; on a narrow screen the parts stack vertically.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Home page. The Device ID is blurred in this picture.

Radio shows the frequency, mode, filter, receive or transmit, and whether CI-V is working. Device shows the firmware version, WiFi, call sign, Device ID with the licence state, and uptime.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings page in the web interface.

The same settings as on the screen, in four sections: Station, Radio, Network radio server and WiFi. Change what you need and click Save at the bottom. Leave a password field empty to keep the current password.

docs.title: Licence, Info and Firmware
docs.text:
• Licence: Device ID, status, and the activation code field. See Getting started.
  • Info: firmware version, Device ID and the open-source licences.
  • Firmware: install a new firmware file. See Getting started.
Info page (top). The Device ID is blurred in this picture.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
In the web interface, while the frequency keypad is open:

Key Does 0 to 9, . Type the frequency. Enter Tune (ENT). Backspace Delete one digit. Delete Clear the entry (CE). Esc Close the panel.
